title: Morning Brief
intro_md: Type "more on G3" (or any code) in April's chat, or tap More info on an item and paste the request there, and I'll dig into it.

items.headline_md: Putin reportedly floats a Trump–Xi–Putin summit on Ukraine, without Zelenskyy
items.summary_md: The WSJ says Putin raised the idea in an Oct. 9 call with Trump, possibly for November's APEC summit in Shenzhen; Rubio said there's been talk of a meeting but nothing finalized. Overnight Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area and 200+ drones nationwide, leaving at least 550,000 households without power, per Zelenskyy.

items.headline_md: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured in a 'deliberate' car ramming
items.summary_md: An SUV struck the 65-year-old independent outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria; bystanders held the 43-year-old driver and police found a knife in his car. PM Albanese called it a deliberate act, and the counterterrorism squad has been activated.

items.headline_md: Italy: Meloni calls an emergency meeting after weekend cost-of-living riots in Milan
items.summary_md: Police used tear gas and water cannon in Milan as more than 200 people were detained, 80% of them minors, with disorder also in Turin and Bologna. It follows the violent protests in France covered yesterday.

items.headline_md: Alberta votes today on whether to start a process toward a separation referendum
items.summary_md: If voters say yes, a binding referendum on leaving Canada could come as soon as 2027; polls suggest most Albertans want to stay. Counting starts no earlier than 7 PM AZ tonight, with results expected early Tuesday.

items.headline_md: Yemen: reports detail Iran's IRGC helping the Houthis as attacks on Saudi cities mount
items.summary_md: The WSJ reported Mahan Air flights carried IRGC officers, drone parts and missile guidance systems to the Houthis, who now control Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandeb strait. A recent Houthi strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed 13.

items.headline_md: WFP cuts Gaza food aid by about a third over funding shortages
items.summary_md: The UN agency says the number of people it helps in Gaza will drop from 1.6 million to 1.1 million.

items.headline_md: China's economy grew 4.5% in Q3 as AI-driven exports offset weak spending at home
items.summary_md: That's up from the prior quarter's three-year low but at the bottom of Beijing's 4.5%-5% target; high-tech goods sales rose 14.3% while property investment fell more than 20% over nine months.

items.headline_md: French unrest hits French bonds, stocks and the euro
items.summary_md: France's 10-year yield jumped more than 10 basis points, the CAC 40 fell about 1.3% and the euro slipped 0.28% against the dollar, with the French-German yield gap near euro-crisis levels. Investors doubt PM Lecornu's minority government can pass a credible 2027 budget.

items.headline_md: Musk says he will give one SpaceX share to every U.S. child next year
items.summary_md: CNBC puts that at roughly $10.5 billion of stock at Friday's $146.03 close, though Musk gave no details on how it would work. It came right after Anthropic's public-benefit-fund pledge (see A1).

items.headline_md: Supercell completes its buyout of Merge Mansion maker Metacore
items.summary_md: Merge Mansion, estimated at about $490M lifetime revenue (AppMagic), joins Supercell's live portfolio with the goal of getting back to the top of the charts; terms weren't disclosed.

items.headline_md: Activision QA union (AQAU-CWA) votes to authorize a strike
items.summary_md: The roughly 600-member union says Activision has stalled first-contract talks for two years over wages, AI guardrails and contractor use. Activision says it has made progress, offered to meet Oct. 21-22, and has plans so players and releases aren't disrupted.

items.headline_md: Power to the Players Act: a new bill would make buying a game mean owning it
items.summary_md: Rep. Ritchie Torres's bill would have the FTC guarantee ownership rather than a license and require an offline mode before servers shut down, citing NBA 2K25's Dec. 31 shutdown.

items.headline_md: Samson developer Liquid Swords files for bankruptcy
items.summary_md: Staff at the studio behind Samson had reportedly gone unpaid for two months.

sections.title: Video Game Emulation
sections.body_md: Wii U lifter watch: still not public. Mindstormman's GitHub still shows 0 public repos, and GitHub searches only turned up per-game Wii U recomps already seen, no general PowerPC-to-x86 lifter. Reddit blocked this run (403 on old.reddit and www RSS for r/decomps and r/emulation). No verified PS5 or Switch 2 commercial-game breakthrough overnight; KytyPS5 posted routine nightlies only.

items.headline_md: Update: Driveclub Recomp v0.2.3 gets about 15% faster, and rival DCport adds FSR 4
items.summary_md: Driveclub Recomp (OverkillLabs3) runs the PS4 game's own x86-64 code natively on Windows with Vulkan, now hitting ~71 fps vs 62 in a CPU-heavy race, with DLAA/FSR 3.1 AA and up to 8K. The separate DCport adds FSR 4 and FSR 3 frame generation; both are unfinished, offline-only and need your own dump.

items.headline_md: BlueWake 0.8.0: the GameCube Wind Waker PC recomp gets the Wind Waker HD look
items.summary_md: The release adds HD textures built from your own Wind Waker HD copy, faster defaults on Windows and Linux, and an experimental Android build; it needs your own US (GZLE01) disc. Published 7:27 PM AZ Saturday.

items.headline_md: Metroid Prime native PC port 0.30.0 adds remastered effects and cuts Android memory use
items.summary_md: The PrimeDecomp-based port for Windows, Linux and Android adds suit-matched morph balls, the full Flaahgra theme, a beam-stacking option and savestate/door fixes; it needs your own disc. Published 2:42 PM AZ Sunday.

items.headline_md: Eternal Darkness Recomp 0.9.3 adds third- and first-person cameras
items.summary_md: The native Mac/Windows/Linux recomp of the GameCube game adds a beta camera mode beside the original fixed angles; it works only with the European (GEDP01) disc. Published 11:59 AM AZ Sunday.

items.headline_md: Update: Analogue Super Nt+ and Mega Sg+ FPGA console pre-orders open today
items.summary_md: Pre-orders for Analogue's revived SNES and Genesis FPGA consoles, announced last week, open Oct. 19.

items.headline_md: Quick hits: Lost Odyssey Recomp 1.0.6 and a fresh Wind Waker HD Recomp devel build
items.summary_md: Lost Odyssey Recomp 1.0.6 (9:32 PM AZ Sunday) fixes a macOS frame-generation crash and cutscene audio mixing; the Wind Waker HD Recomp posted a new devel build at 3:32 AM AZ today with no new tagged release since v0.3.0.

items.headline_md: Update: Street Fighter opens at No. 1 with $31M (Oct. 16-18) and $51.1M worldwide
items.summary_md: Sunday estimates show the Capcom adaptation drew a mostly older male crowd, a B- CinemaScore and 41% on Rotten Tomatoes; its budget is reportedly under $100M.

items.headline_md: Update: You Can See Everything opens to $15M on just 855 screens, the second-best documentary debut ever
items.summary_md: A24's three-hour Elizabeth Holmes doc had 2,000+ sellouts, 99% on Rotten Tomatoes and a record 4.8 on Letterboxd; it goes wider next weekend.

items.headline_md: Whalefall sinks with $8M; Sense and Sensibility opens to $7.25M
items.summary_md: Disney/20th Century's $60M Whalefall lost the male audience to Street Fighter. The overall weekend hit $103.9M, up 41.9% from the same frame in 2025, and Resident Evil has now reached $148.5M.

items.headline_md: This Friday: DC's R-rated Clayface is tracking around $20M-$29M
items.summary_md: Box Office Theory's latest pinpoint is $26M; Laika's Wildwood sits at 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, while Taika Waititi's Klara and the Sun has poor early reviews (25%).

items.headline_md: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new "public benefit fund"
items.summary_md: Pending shareholder approval, the fund could grow by 2% for every 50% rise in Anthropic's value and might fund nonprofits, direct payouts, or efforts to address AI job losses; governance details come later.

items.headline_md: Update: Disney will hire most of bankrupt Character.AI's staff
items.summary_md: A court filing shows Disney offering jobs to at least 60 Character.AI employees, about $60M a year in pay, as part of a stalking-horse bid that a rival could still top.

items.headline_md: Microsoft pulls out of Nscale's planned UK AI data centre in Essex
items.summary_md: Microsoft had said it would fund a supercomputer at the £2bn Loughton site, whose grid connection has reportedly slipped to the 2030s; Nscale says it's still building.

items.headline_md: Mexico gives Apple, Google, Meta and other platforms 30 days to protect minors
items.summary_md: A presidential decree requires social and streaming platforms to shield kids from harmful content, and Sheinbaum backs a bill to penalize companies that don't comply.

items.headline_md: Apple's foldable iPhone Duo is backordered into January
items.summary_md: Ship dates slipped within a minute of Friday pre-orders, and 9to5Mac says it is likely a mix of strong demand and tight hinge-related supply.

items.headline_md: Futures rebound: Nasdaq 100 +1%, S&P 500 +0.4%, Dow -0.3% (4:48 AM AZ)
items.summary_md: The rebound follows last week's AI selloff, when the Nasdaq lost 4.5% and the S&P nearly 2%.

items.headline_md: Premarket movers: CoreWeave +6%, Intel +3%, AMD and Micron +3% (4:48 AM AZ)
items.summary_md: Intel rose on a JPMorgan upgrade, and CoreWeave bounced after its biggest one-week drop since November 2025.

items.headline_md: Brent slips about 1% to around $108 and WTI is near $101 (4:48 AM AZ); Europe is lower
items.summary_md: Oil is easing off five-month highs after Trump waived Russia sanctions. The Stoxx 600 is down 0.82% and France's CAC 40 down 1.35%.

items.headline_md: Gold $4,171.65 (1:53 AM AZ); bitcoin $82,305, ether $2,420 (5:08 AM AZ)
items.summary_md: Spot gold rose 0.2% as softer oil eased inflation worries ahead of next week's Fed meeting. Crypto prices are Coinbase spot.

items.headline_md: Phoenix: mostly sunny, high near 88, low around 69, dry
items.summary_md: East-southeast wind around 5 mph, with only a 2-7% chance of precipitation all day and no measurable rain forecast. No active alerts. NWS Phoenix forecast updated 3:56 AM AZ.

items.headline_md: Show Low: showers and storms likely (70%), high near 65, low around 47
items.summary_md: A chance of showers before 8 AM, then showers and thunderstorms likely; NWS grid shows about 0.08 in. of rain 11 AM-5 PM AZ and 0.01 in. 5-11 PM, no snow. Gusts to 20 mph; tonight 40% for storms before 5 AM. No active alerts. NWS Flagstaff forecast updated 3:12 AM AZ.

items.headline_md: Snowflake: showers and storms likely 8 AM-5 PM (60%), high near 69, low around 46
items.summary_md: NWS grid shows about 0.04 in. of rain 11 AM-5 PM AZ and 0.01 in. 5-11 PM, no snow, with gusts to 20 mph; tonight a 20% chance of storms before 11 PM. No active alerts. NWS Flagstaff forecast updated 3:12 AM AZ.

items.headline_md: Inside the OpenAI bugging case: the suspect was messaging a Saudi royal
items.summary_md: CNBC's detailed walk through the prosecutors' filing reads like a spy novel, with hidden USB recorders behind conference-room TVs, a deleted 'OpenAI leave' note and a family flown out on a Saudi-military-paid ticket; it's a sharp look at how seriously AI labs' secrets are now being targeted.
